notes: The session's web-search allowance ran out partway through, so several candidates got one search and then only direct page reads with the kit's honest User-Agent. Aggregator pages (BallotReady, Run for Something) were used only as leads; every website listed was opened and names the candidate and the office or place.

Left out and not worked around: natewillems.com answers scripts with a CAPTCHA redirect, so Nate Willems has no website finding although Wikipedia and BallotReady give that address as his campaign site. carlisleiowa.org's page for Drew Merrifield (a search result described him as Mayor of Carlisle with a term ending December 31, 2025) returned 404, so no office is recorded for him. BallotReady ties a 'Jeff Frost' to the Gilbertville City Council, but nothing opened ties that person to the Black Hawk County supervisor candidate, so it is left out. Matt Schultz's and Wikipedia's birth dates carry no citation and are left out; Wikipedia's article on Schultz says 'Democratic Party' in its opening and 'Republican' in its box, so no party finding was taken from it.

The Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee's pages for Matt Robinson (HD-72) and Andrew Fitzgerald (HD-98) list them as target races but do not use the word endorse, so no endorsement is recorded. No party's own endorsement page was found for anyone in this part.

Nothing found beyond the filing for Jeff Frost, Jeff Staton, Drew Merrifield, Michael Coonrad (social media pages only), and sitting legislators David A. Sieck, Brooke Boden, Skyler Wheeler, Mark I. Thompson, Dave Jacoby and Heather Hora (no campaign site of their own was found).

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every url was re-opened with the kit's reader. Wikipedia's opening line calls Matt Schultz a member of the Democratic Party while its box says Republican; no party finding rests on it. Jeff Kulmatycki's county findings were removed for want of a second anchor, not because the page was wrong.
